env_checkpoint_policy.rule: 05.4-01's A/B showed DreamShaper XL alpha2 won on the floor tile (richer ember glow, better flagstone framing) but regressed only on rembg-cutout props (shadow-blob / stray-axle artifacts on the wheel subject). Non-cutout kinds (floor tiles, tile variants, wall faces/strips) are generated with the dreamshaper_xl_alpha2 profile; cutout kinds (props, columns, gates, wall caps, decals, hazard-skins) are generated under the sdxl_base default. The mechanism is the per-call `gen_subject.py`/`gen_batch.py --ckpt-profile dreamshaper_xl_alpha2` override (existing config flag, no code change) run against explicit key lists for just the floor_a/floor_b/wallface subjects of each biome -- NOT a global env_checkpoint toggle, since that leaves ambient state that a crashed/interrupted process could strand (this happened once during this plan's execution and was caught and reverted). Because --ckpt-profile suffixes the raw filename ({key}_s{seed}_dreamshaper_xl_alpha2.png) and env_build.py._raw_paths expects the unsuffixed name, the accepted DreamShaper raw file for each of these 3 subjects per biome is copied (not moved -- the suffixed original stays as the reproducibility record) to the unsuffixed {key}_s{seed}.png path once self_review/cultural_check pass, immediately before running env_build.py. The top-level env_checkpoint value stays sdxl_base at all times; it is never toggled globally. If a DreamShaper tile fails the seamless/readability checks (D-08 tile_limits or a visible 2x2 seam), that asset falls back to sdxl_base (plain --attempt rerun, no --ckpt-profile) and is regenerated under the default checkpoint instead.
